title: PT-4435: Show a visible connection-lost state when the socket dies

reviews.author: katherinejensen00
reviews.bodyText:
Second review pass
Re-reviewed after the Alert/Radix rewrite. Almost everything below is a consequence of that rewrite being made from code-review findings without the result ever being rendered — so I'd treat "look at it running" as the top action item, not a formality.
Blocking
The keyboard-containment test doesn't test containment. overlay-connection-lost.component.test.tsx:196-201
Verified by mutation: changing the component to <Dialog open modal={false}> — which disables Radix's trapFocus — leaves all 12 tests in the file green. Removing the Dialog entirely fails only at line 194 (expect(reload).toHaveFocus()), which is autofocus, not containment. So the suite pins "something focuses Reload" and nothing else.
Cause is environmental: userEvent.tab() doesn't move focus out of a DialogContent in this jsdom setup even with modal={false}, though it moves normally between two plain buttons.
A falsifiable proxy does exist and flips with modal: Radix's hideOthers stamps `aria-hidden=" a real-browser interaction test, would restore the guarantee. As it stands, the one behavior the ADR chose Radix for is unverified.
Rendering bugs introduced by the Alert composition
1. The Reload button will overlap the banner text. overlay-connection-lost.component.tsx:181
AlertAction is tw:absolute tw:top-2 tw:end-2 (alert.tsx:89) — outside the alert's grid flow — and the only space reserved for it is tw:has-data-[slot=alert-action]:pe-18 on the Alert base (alert.tsx:12), i.e. 72px, less the 8px end-2 offset = 64px of clearance.
button sits at about y=8-36px inside the alert, spanning the title row and the first line of the description.
Maximized and in English the description happens not to reach that far. Below roughly 750px, or in any locale with a longer label, the first line wraps out to the padding edge and runs under the button. The Alert action slot is built for a short action like "Retry" or an icon, not a two-or-three-word label on a full-window-width strip.
2. asChild silently defeats the destructive description colour. overlay-connection-lost.component.tsx:178
Radix Slot merges as {...slotProps, ...childProps}, so DialogDescription's data-slot="dialog-description" reaches AlertDescription as a prop and is spread after its own data-slot="alert-description" (atw:text-muted-foreground.
Result: a destructive-tinted strip with a text-destructive title and a plain muted-grey message, which is the weakest contrast pairing on this banner, dark mode especially. The id / aria-labelledby / aria-describedby wiring is unaffected and does work.
Fix is either className="tw:text-destructive/90" on AlertDescription at the call site, or restoring data-slot="alert-description" on the child.
ENGLISH_FALLBACKS[CONNECTION_LOST_MESSAGE_KEY] is the un-expanded template. The component runs it through formatReplacementString before passing it down; the stories pass it straight through. The comment two lines above ("so the stories cannot drift from the text the app actually renders") currently asserts the opposite of what the file does.
Worth fixing before anyone follows the PR's own review-focus list, which sends the reviewer to exactly these two stories.
DialogContent unconditionally renders DialogOverlay (dialog.tsx:110-113), so a tw:bg-black/10 + backdrop-blur-xs layer at z-index 450 sits under this component's tw:bg-background/70 at 800 — a compounded blur-then-wash treatment that hasn't been looked at.
The comment explaining this is also inaccurate: DialogOverlay does accept and merge style (dialog.tsx:59-72). What's missing is a way for DialogContent to forward one — it forwards overlayClassName, which would let you neutralize the built-in backdrop from here.
The override string doesn't cancel DialogContent's tw:data-open:zoom-in-95, and nothing in it conflicts, so tailwind-merge keeps it. For about 100ms the full-viewport scrim is drawn at 95% scale about its centre — a band of un-dimmed, still-live-looking app around all four edges. tw:data-open:zoom-in-100, or dropping animate-in here, fixes it. FirstRunOverlay has the same gap, so fixing both keeps the two gates consistent.
Design gaps
ConnectionLostOverlayPresentational and FirstRunGate are both Radix modal Dialogs, and Radix's DismissableLayer and FocusScope arbitrate by mount order, not z-index. z-index only decides what is visible.
So if the first-run gate mounts after the connection-lost state, the connection-lost scrim is the only thing visible (800 > 700), but its Reload button gets pointer-events: none and the focus trap sits in the invisible wizard behind the scrim — where the error effect actively calls retryButtonRef.current?.focus() (first-run-overlay.component.tsx:1resolveInternal seeds { kind: 'app' } and then runs startBackgroundRegistrationRecheck() (first-run-store.ts:236), which can re-raise the gate at any later moment, including after the socket has died. Same for waitForRegistration → applyStatus({ kind: 'error' }) (first-run-store.ts:266) resolving late off a probe that was in flight when the connection dropped.
The ADR's reasoning for 800 > 700 is right; the mechanism just doesn't implement it. Options are suppressing other app-gating modals once the connection-lost state latches, or keyboard-shortcuts.data.ts:148
A Radix FocusScope constrains where DOM focus lands; it doesn't stop handlers bound above or outside the focused element. Two categories still fire while the scrim is up:

Main-process before-input-event handlers (main.ts:1295-1332) intercept keys before any renderer frame sees them: F12, Ctrl+Tab / Ctrl+Shift+Tab, and the PT9 verse-navigation set (F8/Ctrl+F8, F9/Ctrl+F9, Ctrl+Up/Down, Ctrl+B). All travel over the dead
notification-display.tsx:104 registers a document-level keydown for Alt+T, which bubbles from the dialog content regardless of focus scope.

That's the silent-failure mode this feature exists to end, reached by keyboard instead of pointer. Gating the first category needs main to know the renderer has latched, which cuts against the renderer-local design — so documenting the gap may well be the right call, but the entry, the component doc block, and the ADR's "Keyboard gate" bullet currently overstate what's covered.
The documented startup race follows from wiring the subscription in a React effect, and the ADR justifies it by citing initWorkspaceUpdatingService. But src/renderer/index.tsx starts three renderer-lifetime subscriptions — initAutoSyncBlockingService(), initAutoSyncEditBlockDriver(), initSyncActivityService() — directly in the startup IIFE, with comments saying they return unsubscribers deliberately never called. That's exactly this store's shape.
Moving the call there, or subscribing at module-import time in the store (the emitter exists at module load
9. Main already solved the quit-time false positive. rpc-client.ts:387
rpc-server.ts:325 computes const diedDuringShutdown = !isClean && isAppShuttingDown(); from shutdown-latch.service. The client end has no equivalent — isCleanCloseEvent rejects 1006 identically whether the network broke or the app is quitting. So on an ordinary quit the store latches and the overlay is asked to render, and whether the user sees a flash depends only on paint timingignore losses once set. Worth doing rather than leaving as a timing-dependent invisible.
Documentation accuracy
10. The PR is no longer mergeable. git rev-list --count HEAD..origin/main reports 2 (8f230e863b9 PT-4325, 55a5c54dcf1 PT-4240), and GitHub reports mergeable: CONFLICTING / mergeStateStatus: DIRTY. The body still says "0 commits behind main and mergeable". Conflicts are most likely the commdark, while the same body says the screenshots predate the review because the banner moved onto Alert`, and the review section says nothing was run in the live app. Findings 1-5 are what that gap cost.
12. The ADR's Signal section describes code that no longer exists. Architecture-Decisions.md:2879
It declares PlatformEvent<undefined> (all four declarations ship PlatformEvent<void>), says "the payload is undefined on purpose", and quotes the emission verbatim as irelays "using the same shape as the existing onDidDisconnectClientrelay immediately above it", but the same review round extracted both intorelayWhileUp`, so there's no duplicated shape to mirror. Line citations are stale throughout (export is at 156 not 158; subscription at 224 not 199).
This log gets read for precedent by people and by pt10-reuse-scout, so a wrong snippet propagates.
**13. The ADR leaves its own open future reader can tell the check happened.
14. The toolbar-height rationale is contradicted by the overlay's own imports. toolbar-height.util.ts:10
The comment says the constants couldn't live in platform-dock-layout-positioning.util.ts because the overlay can't reach the clearance "through a module that pulls in the network services". But the overlay already does, transitively: `overlay-connection-lost.componentdirectly.
The real invariant is that no PAPI round trip happens on the reaction path — the hooks resolved while the socket was alive and their values persist. A dead websocket doesn't make an imported module fail. The actual reason to avoid the positioning util is the dialogs-barrel import cycle its own header describes, which is what dock-tab-group.util.ts was extracted for.
Flagging this specifically becauseasserts the reaction path makes no PAPI call and no lint rule constrains imports, so it's one convenience import away from silent regression.
Smaller items

alert.tsx:87 — AlertAction becomes public API here, and its only TSDoc is @inheritdoc Alert, which resolves to a description of Alert. Nothing tells a consumer it positions children absolutely, must be a child of Alert, or that Alert reserves its space via pe-18 so an action rendered outside it will overlap.toolbar") is unqualified on the Power-mode value.
rpc.interface.ts:148 — required rather than optional is the right call. But the sibling onDidDisconnectClient (119-133) carries an explicit "platform-internal core plumbing, not part of the @papi/* surface" note and the new member drops it, and both are emitted verbatim into papi.d.ts.
connection-lost-store.ts:53 — @internal trails prose on the same line, so tooling parses it as body text and the export isn't actually marked internal.
overlay-connection-lost.componeuse-backend-sync-activity.hook.ts:32), and it re-reads on subscribe, closing by construction the gap the manual syncState()` handles by hand.
overlay-connection-lost.component.tsx:235 — localizedOrEnglish(KEY, localizedStrings[KEY]) written four times, each passing the same key twice.
connection-lost-store.ts — the sibling pair splits state from wiring (workspace-updating-store.ts has zero imports; workspace-updating-service.ts does the network subscription). Collapsing both into one module is why app.component.test.tsx had to mock the store outright. The bespoke store
keyboard-shortcuts.data.ts:146 — the entry documents Tab containment, which is Radix's default in every Dialog and isn't catalogued for any of them including the first-run gate. Meanwhile the handler this PR actually adds — onEscapeKeyDown prevented at component.tsx:146, making Escape inert where it closes every other dialog — isn't documented, and the dismiss-overlays entry says "A modal dialog on top is left to its own shell", so a reader has no way to learn this one swallows it.
network.service.test.ts:101 — the double still models the subscriber as (event: undefined) => void. It's laundered through as unknown as, so nothing type-checks it against
Test counts are per-file rather than per-test: network.service.test.ts has 6 it blocks of which 3 are new, app.component.test.tsx 7 of which 2 are new. New tests total 31, not 39, and neither file is a new suite.
The "Things to scrutinise" bullet says the scrim "blocks keyboard as well as pointer". The scrim blocks pointers; containment comes from FocusScope. The ADR, doc block and catalog entry all say it correctly — just that bullet still describes the hand-rolled behaviour.

On the design
The core call is sound and the reasoning is unusually well recorded. The no-PAPI-on-the-reaction-path constraint is the right one, mounting unconditionally from startup so the hooks resolve while the socket is alive is the right consequence, and latching without a false transition is right given no reconnect exists. Findings 6 through 9 are all cases where the implementation doesn't yet deliver something the ADR correctly argues for, not cases where the argument is wrong.

Findings 6 through 9 are all cases where the implementation doesn't yet deliver something the ADR correctly argues for, not cases where the argument is wrong.
Review was AI-assisted (multi-perspective pass). Line references and the mergeability claim were checked against the branch; the button-width numbers in finding 1 are estimated from class definitions rather than measured.
Two things I'd flag as yours to weigh rather than the author's: whether the "Reload anyway" label plus no dismissal path is enough (Ryan's call unconditionally from startup so the hooks resolve while the socket is alive is the right consequence, and latching without a false transition is right given no reconnect exists. PR #2742 — Round 3 Review Summary
PT-4435: Show a visible connection-lost state when the socket dies
Reviewed at 8ff695c54ace124c7605a74ffa6eae7430cea848 · 2026-09-08 · not posted to GitHub
Full detail: pr-review-2742-round3.md. Round 2's report is preserved at pr-review-2742.md.
Verdict: 1 blocking, 15 warnings, 16 suggestions. Seven perspectives (security, scope, ux,
contracts, tests, architecture, clarity), each given both prior rounds as a dedup list and told to
verify the claimed fixes rather than trust them.

Verified as genuinely fixed
Recorded so round 4 doesn't re-check them. Established by mutation or by reading the code, not from
the author's response.

Round 2's blocking finding is properly fixed. With modal={false} the suite now goes red with
exactly one failure — the aria-hidden containment assertion, not autofocus. That is the
separation round 2 asked for.
The quit-time guard is well covered by tests (separate from whether it fires in production —
see W1). Dropping the shutdown latch turns 3 tests red; both orderings are pinned.
Rendering fixes 1–4 verified mechanism by mechanism, including running the repo's own
extendTailwindMerge({prefix:'tw'}) to confirm the grid and backdrop overrides actually collapse.
All four contract fixes landed; papi.d.ts and platform-bible-react/dist/ verified in sync
with source; AlertAction genuinely un-exported.
"37 tests" verified exactly, cross-checked two ways.
The reaction path is genuinely PAPI-free, with no injection surface and no secrets.

Tree confirmed clean at the PR head after every mutation run.

Blocking
B1 — Banner text fails WCAG AA in the Platform dark theme
src/renderer/components/overlays/overlay-connection-lost.component.tsx:224
Round 2 asked for the destructive description colour to be restored. Restating
data-slot="alert-description" did that — and put the copy onto a token the codebase explicitly
documents as not text-grade. lib/platform-bible-react/src/index.css:73:

--diff-deleted added — text-grade red … --destructive is background-grade in Platform dark.

.dark sets --destructive: oklch(0.396 0.1331 25.71) (≈ red-900). Against the banner's ground:



Element
Token
Contrast




Title
tw:text-destructive
≈ 2.0:1


Description
tw:text-destructive/90
≈ 1.8:1



AA needs 4.5:1. The pre-fix text-muted-foreground was ≈ 8:1 there, so the fix made the message
strictly harder to read. Light Platform is better but still short (≈ 3.3:1). .paratext-dark is fine.
Blocking because this is the screen a user reaches when nothing else in the app works, and reading it
is the entire point of the feature. One-token fix at the call site: --diff-deleted is the token the
theme provisions for exactly this, or use an opaque destructive ground with
text-destructive-foreground, or fall back to tw:text-foreground.

Considered and deliberately not called blocking

Quit-time latch never arms on quit (W1). main.ts calls newWindow.destroy() on the
isAppGoingDown branch, and its own comment says destroy() skips beforeunload; pagehide is
in the same skipped sequence. So markShuttingDown() runs only when the app stays up. Behaviour
is no worse than before — the banner is still kept off-screen by teardown timing — but the code
comment, store doc, and ADR now all assert a guarantee that doesn't hold. Documentation defect.
First-run stand-down has zero coverage (W3). Deleting the line leaves 139/139 green. The code
is correct; only the pin is missing. Blocking-adjacent, since the late-raise path is what a
refactor breaks silently and the failure mode is severe (Reload visible, focus trapped in an
invisible wizard).
zoom-in-100 doesn't override zoom-in-95 (W2). Genuinely unfixed rather than merely
undocumented, but the symptom is a ~100ms band of un-dimmed app during the open animation.


The rest, by theme
Correctness / behaviour

W2 — tailwind-merge has no class group for tw-animate-css, so both zoom classes ship and
stylesheet source order decides. The live measurement can't detect this (animate-in sets no
fill-mode, so the transform reads none afterwards either way). Round-2 finding 5 is unverified.
W4 — the documented keyboard gap omits PlatformMenubar's five document-level Alt hotkeys, which
pull focus out of the FocusScope and open a menu whose items dispatch over the dead socket. It's
the one category that is renderer-local, so it needs no main→renderer relay to close.
W5 — OverlayHost/OverlayModalDialog didn't get the stand-down FirstRunOverlay got; a
showDialog in flight when the socket dies mounts after and takes the focus trap. Narrow window;
the two reviewers disagreed on reachability.

Tests

W3 above, plus: the seam test's not.toHaveBeenCalled() is a negative assertion with nothing to be
a negative of; the scrim test mirrors four Tailwind class names; index.tsx's module-scope
ordering constraint is carried only by a comment. At PR level — real keyboard containment is now
pinned by an aria-hidden proxy plus a one-off manual CDP pass, and e2e-tests/ gained nothing.

Documentation drift (the bulk of the warnings)

W7 — merging this turns twelve existing TODO(PT-4435) markers into pointers at a closed ticket
that deliberately didn't do the reconnect work; three say "when PT-4435 lands, drop the .fails".
W8 — the ADR's "line numbers are deliberately omitted" is contradicted by four surviving citations,
three already stale on this commit.
W9 — the PR body drifted again in four places: two "Things to scrutinise" bullets describe risks
the branch already closed; the scope list omits first-run-overlay.component.tsx and still cites
the withdrawn AlertAction export; "0 commits behind main" is stale for the second round; and the
ADR conflict resolution is described as "append order", which the append-model-is-dead ADR in this
very diff forbids (outcome was right, method described is wrong).
W12–W15 — tests deferring coverage to a non-existent docs/superpowers/plans/; a doc paragraph
over-generalizing what needs main's involvement; an ADR reference to the non-existent
initConnectionLostStore(); three deferrals with no grep-able marker.

Merge readiness

W10 — conflicting with main again, 1 commit behind. Conflicts are only the committed
dist/index.cjs and dist/index.js bundles: resolve by rm -rf dist + rebuild, not by
hand-merging. HEAD is also a merge commit, not a rebase, despite the body saying "rebased".


Suggested next steps

Fix B1 — one token, and it's the feature's whole point.
Decide W1: correct the comment/doc/ADR to say the latch covers window-close and reload only, or
defer the quit case to the follow-up ticket.
Add the first-run stand-down test (W3) — cheap, and it guards a severe failure mode.
Make the zoom cancellation deterministic (W2), here and in first-run-overlay.component.tsx:58.
File the follow-up ticket so W7's twelve TODOs and W15's three deferrals get a real ID.
Sync with main and rebuild dist/.
Reconcile the PR body with the diff before a human reviewer reads it (W9).

PR #2742 — Round 4
PT-4435: Show a visible connection-lost state when the socket dies
Head reviewed: dbf262cf755 · 2026-09-08
Verdict: 2 blocking, 3 warnings.
Two notes first, neither your fault:

You're right that W6 and W11 never reached you — round 3's posted summary skipped both. W6 is
below; W11 (the autodocs page renders two modal Radix dialogs into one iframe, giving an
unscrollable untabbable docs page) is real but pre-existing in shape —
first-run-overlay.stories.tsx:21 already does the same on main — so it can go to the
follow-up.
Everything you claimed to fix, held up under mutation. W2, W3, W5, W8, W12, W13, the
tailwind-merge collapse, the artifact sync (papi.d.ts is +45/−0, so nothing main carried was
dropped; dist/ export set 269 → 270, zero removed) and the localization test's falsifiability
were all verified mechanically, not taken on trust. The findings below are new or were never
delivered.


Blocking
1. The main merge silently broke the feature on a refused startup connection
src/client/services/rpc-client.ts:380-435
The dbf262cf merge brought in #2737, which rewrote the same two files this PR touches. Git
auto-merged them textually, not semantically:

#2737 added failConnectionAttempt(...) to onError (rpc-client.ts:388).
AsyncVariable.rejectWithReason calls its rejecter synchronously (async-variable.ts:105).
So await this.connectionComplete.promise in connect() resumes on the microtask right after
the error task — before the browser dispatches close.
connect()'s catch runs removeEventListenersFromWebSocket() (rpc-client.ts:222).
onWebSocketClose never runs. The emitter never fires.




Startup shape
Result




Connection refused (error then close) — the exact #2737 incident
Silent. No overlay; app renders with raw localize keys and no data.


TCP accepted, dropped before the websocket upgrade (close, no error)
Overlay shows



This worked before the merge: onError only logged, so connect() stayed parked on the 10s
timeout and close arrived first. The feature is now non-deterministic at startup, decided by
whether an error happened to precede the close, and neither branch has a test.
Fix — pick one and pin it. rpc.interface.ts:147-164 says the event fires when this process
"loses" its connection, and you can't lose one you never had. Gating the emit on
connectionStatus === ConnectionStatus.Connected makes both shapes agree on silent and matches
that contract — startup failure then stays invisible, but that's #2737's territory and
PT-4494/PT-4495 own it. Covering the never-connected case instead means moving the emit out of the
error/close race.
2. B1 reopened — the banner still fails AA in both light themes
src/renderer/components/overlays/overlay-connection-lost.component.tsx:225
The --diff-deleted swap is correctly wired and does fix both dark themes. The measurement was
against --background, but the banner's real ground is that composited with tw:bg-destructive/10
— a tint costing ~0.6:1, which is exactly the margin. Title is 14px font-medium, description
14px, so both need 4.5:1.



Theme
Title
Description /90




Platform light
4.18 FAIL
3.99 FAIL


paratext-light
3.99 FAIL
3.81 FAIL


Platform dark
6.74 pass
5.62 pass


paratext-dark
6.10 pass
5.17 pass



Two independent computations agree to within 0.01. Note paratext-light is unchanged at 3.99 /
3.81 — it was already red-600 via --destructive, so the fix did nothing there.
Two options: drop tw:bg-destructive/10 (the wrapper already has an opaque bg-background;
border + icon still carry the tone) — clears AA everywhere at 4.52 worst case, no token change, no
UX sign-off; or darken light-theme --diff-deleted to red-700 — 5.64 / 5.37, real headroom, but
it's a theme-token change and index.css's header requires UX approval. Either way, the in-code
comment claiming "clears AA in all four" needs correcting.

Warnings
3. index.startup-order.test.ts is a false green
src/renderer/index.startup-order.test.ts:21-27
indexOf('initConnectionLostService()') matches inside comments. Demonstrated by mutation:
// initConnectionLostService(); // moved into a React effect in app.component.tsx
The substring stays at the same early offset, so both assertions hold. The feature is fully
unwired from renderer startup and all 59 tests across the PR's 11 files pass — including the test
nominated as the pin for this exact constraint. A clean rename does fail it, but a commented-out
line or a breadcrumb comment is at least as likely a refactor artifact.
Fix — anchor to a statement and prove there's exactly one (^ at column 0 also pins module
scope, which is the real constraint):
const calls = source.match(/^initConnectionLostService\(\);$/gm) ?? [];
expect(calls).toHaveLength(1);
4. The overlay-host late-open test can silently become vacuous
src/renderer/components/overlay-host.component.test.tsx:82-93
You correctly rewrote it to drive the host's own store listener — but the listener is captured into
notifyOverlaysChanged and invoked as notifyOverlaysChanged?.(), and nothing asserts it was ever
captured. Demonstrated: delete subscribe(syncOverlays) from the effect and all three tests stay
green. The connected-case test doesn't catch it because it's served by the effect's initial
syncOverlays(), not the subscription. (The sibling first-run suite isn't exposed this way — it has
a positive control for its read path.)
Fix: expect(notifyOverlaysChanged).toBeDefined(); before the act() and drop the ?. — or
drive the connected case through the same seam.
5. W6 (never delivered) — and the {@link} it leans on is dead in the published output
src/shared/services/network.service.ts:147-156 → lib/papi-dts/papi.d.ts:2769-2778
onDidDisconnectClient (127-145) carries both the "not part of the @papi/* surface" note and the
full never-fires-elsewhere explanation. onDidLoseConnection (147-155) carries neither — it
compresses to "Local to this process" and defers to a {@link}.
That link doesn't resolve. The generated declare module 'shared/services/network.service' imports
RpcClientDisconnectEvent but not IRpcMethodRegistrar, because the source only uses that type in
the non-exported let jsonRpc (network.service.ts:119), so the dts bundler drops it. On the
public papi-dts site the event's sole explanation renders as literal unlinked text.
A main-process subscriber reads the declaration they actually import, sees "Fires when this
process's own connection to the network is lost unexpectedly", subscribes, and gets an event that
can never fire there. Fix: inline the two sentences from rpc.interface.ts:150-157 — closes
both halves.

Deferred to the follow-up
Not worth another round: the ADR says three sites carry TODO(main-renderer-shutdown-relay) but
grep finds two (the extension-host case has no marker — worth fixing before merge since

reviews.author: jolierabideau
reviews.bodyText:
Round 4 addressed at 85fb507b93a. Full detail in this comment; summary here so the review thread carries it.
Both blocking findings fixed, each verified before changing anything:

#1, the startup emit race — confirmed. AsyncVariable.rejectWithReason calls its rejecter synchronously (async-variable.ts:105), so on a refused connection connect()'s catch resumes on the microtask before the browser dispatches close and strips the listeners; onWebSocketClose never ran. Took your first option: the emit is gated on connectionStatus === Connected, which is what onDidLoseConnection already promised. Both startup shapes are pinned, and the gate is falsifiable — replacing it with if (true) turns exactly those two tests red.
#2, B1 reopened — confirmed. I recomputed the contrast table from the oklch tokens and reproduced your numbers to within 0.01, including that paratext-light was unchanged at 3.99 / 3.81 because its --diff-deleted and --destructive are the same red-600. Dropped tw:bg-destructive/10; worst case across all four themes is 4.52. Verified with the repo's own extendTailwindMerge({prefix:'tw'}) that the override actually collapses the variant's bg-card.

All three warnings fixed, each by first reproducing your mutation: the startup-order pin is now a column-0 whole-statement match requiring exactly one hit (the commented-out call now fails it); the overlay-host late-open case requires the captured store listener (deleting subscribe now fails it); and network.service's onDidLoseConnection has the two sentences inlined, since IRpcMethodRegistrar is genuinely dropped from that generated module.
Deferred list done: the third TODO(main-renderer-shutdown-relay) site now exists in network.service.ts beside the relay that would carry it, so grep finds the three the ADR claims; the quit-case test prose is corrected in both files; the .fails cases say "when reconnect lands"; and the body's AlertAction sign-off ask is gone along with the two other stale mentions. W11 goes to the follow-up, per your call.
Two things I did not do, deliberately:

Darkening light-theme --diff-deleted to red-700 is the better fix — 5.64 / 5.37 is headroom where 4.52 is a 0.02 pass. I left it because index.css requires UX approval for a token change and this state shouldn't wait on one; it's recorded in the ADR and at the call site as the not-taken option. Your call whether to pull it in.
Covering the never-connected case. The gate means a refused startup stays silent — PT-4494 / PT-4495's territory on your own read, and a reload button is not the answer to a server that was never there. The other half of your fork is a bigger change than a gate; say so if you want it here.

main sync: MERGEABLE, 0 behind. Conflicts were only the dist/ bundles, resolved by rebuild — checked two ways: the rebuilt bundle keeps all 278 exports main carried and adds only Z_INDEX_CONNECTION_LOST, and Architecture-Decisions.md auto-merged to 72 entries, no duplicate slugs, in byte order.
Verification: typecheck clean, lint 0 errors, 3,739 tests pass. One failure, electron-builder-snap-config.test.ts (expects gnome-42-2204, finds gnome-3-28-1804) — pre-existing on main, confirmed by checking origin/main out and running it there; this branch touches no .erb file.
Still yours: the 16 round-3 suggestions have never reached me (round 4 didn't carry them either) — post them and I'll do one pass; the token darkening above; fresh screenshots (browser-only); the follow-up ticket the TODO slugs wait on; and the "Reload anyway" dismissal-path UX call.

reviews.author: katherinejensen00
reviews.bodyText:
Just one blocker introduced by my tour changes. Feel free to push back on it as out of scope. I am approving just in case you want to put this into its own work item.

Real blocker — the onboarding tour isn't stood down. tour.component.tsx:414, window-capture Escape → stopPropagation() + onSkip() → writeTourDone() → a localStorage flag that survives the reload. Press Esc at the connection-lost banner and you permanently lose an onboarding tour you never saw. That's irreversible user-visible state loss, triggered by the most obvious key to press, in the exact scenario this feature exists to handle — and the PR's own new catalog entry asserts "Escape is inert while it is shown." I confirmed the whole chain at source. Same gap also makes Tab a dead key (:441). Fix is the one-liner already used twice in this PR.
